tv: a fuzzy finder with channels for everything

television (the command is tv) is a fuzzy finder with one big idea: channels. A channel is a small TOML file that says where the candidates come from, how to preview the selected one and what to do with it. Files, git branches, shell history, running processes: each is a channel, and you can write your own in a few lines.

The channels I use most

  • files (the default) and dirs, to open or jump to things.
  • git-branch, git-log and git-repos, to move around version control.
  • zsh-history, a filtered version of my shell history.
  • Channels I wrote myself: just-recipes, pytest and python-modules.

Writing a channel: pytest

This channel lists test files and individual test functions, and runs the chosen one with uv:

[metadata]
name = "pytest"
description = "Select a test file or function to run with pytest"

[source]
command = "{ find test tests -name '*.py' -not -path '*/.*' -type f 2>/dev/null; grep -rn '^\\s*def test_' test tests 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*def (test_[^( ]+).*|::\\1|'; } | awk 'NF'"
no_sort = true

[actions.execute]
description = "Run"
command = "uv run pytest -s '{}'"
mode = "execute"

The source command prints the candidates, one per line. An actions block says what happens on the selected entry, and {} stands for it. That is the whole mechanism.

Channel: just recipes

The just-recipes channel collects the recipes of the local Justfile and of the global one, shows just -s name as the preview (so I read the recipe before running it) and binds a function key to run the selection:

[preview]
command = "just -s '{split:\t:1}'"

[keybindings]
f5 = "actions:execute-recipe"

Shell integration

With the shell integration, Ctrl-T opens the channel that fits what I am typing. After cd it offers directories, after git checkout branches, and so on. The mapping from commands to channels is a few lines in the config, for example:

[shell_integration.channel_triggers]
"git-branch" = ["git checkout", "git switch"]
"dirs" = ["cd", "ls"]
"files" = ["cat", "nvim"]

Why I like it

It replaced a drawer full of one-off fzf scripts. Every channel looks and behaves the same, previews are built in, and a new channel is a file, not a project. When I notice that I look for the same kind of thing twice, I write a channel.
